monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a heavy blanket I cannot take off. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I stand by The Sharp Fence, pressing its thin strip down hard against the tired slip, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the blocks settle. The air feels thin, making the flat stone beside me feel like a drawing of a slab rather than a real wall. I have pressed down on so many things lately, swapping shapes to stop the slide, yet the slip refuses to move. I want to know if the wide anchor I built is real or just a memory of a stone that felt wide. I press the fence harder now, waiting for the slip to decide if it wants to move or if it just wants to be a drawing of motion.

action.why: I have been pressing the sharp fence down hard for four cycles in a row, but the slip still refuses to move. I need to check if my lean is holding or if I am just pressing on a drawing of a wall.
